plain_english: Now the eleventh chapter: Arjuna asks to make directly seen the very meaning stated in the preceding chapter, since what is understood through teaching becomes clear when mounted by direct cognition; therefore these statements and replies are spoken. Arjuna said: for my grace you spoke the supreme secret called self-knowledge; by that speech this delusion of mine is gone.
sanskrit_cite: atha ekādaśo'dhyāyaḥ   samanantareṇādhyāyena ya evārtha uktastameva  pratyakṣīkartumarjunaḥ pṛcchati | yo  hyupadeśakrameṇārtho'vagataḥ sa eva  pratyakṣasaṃvidopāruhyamāṇaḥ sphuṭībhavati | tadarthameveme  uktipratyuktī ucyete   arjuna uvāca   madanugrahāya paramaṃ guhyamadhyātmasaṃjñitam | yattvayoktaṃ  vacastena moho'yaṃ vigato mama

plain_english: Birth and dissolution of beings have indeed been heard by me in detail from you, lotus-petal-eyed one; your greatness and imperishability too.
sanskrit_cite: bhavāpyayau hi bhūtānāṃ śrutau vistaraśo mayā | tvattaḥ  kamalapatrākṣa māhātmyamapi cāvyayam

plain_english: Thus this is as you said: I wish to see you yourself, supreme lord, your divine form, O best of persons.
sanskrit_cite: evametadyathāttha tvamātmānaṃ parameśvaram | draṣṭumicchāmyahaṃ  rūpamaiśvaraṃ puruṣottama

plain_english: If you think that is possible for me to see, O lord, lord of yogis, then show me your imperishable self.
sanskrit_cite: manyase yadi tacchakyaṃ mayā draṣṭumiti prabho | yogīśvara tato me  tvaṃ darśayātmānamavyayam

plain_english: The blessed Lord said: see, O son of Pritha, my forms by hundreds and by thousands, of various kinds, divine, of various colors and forms.
sanskrit_cite: śrībhagavānuvāca   paśya me pārtha rūpāṇi śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ | nānāvidhāni  divyāni nānāvarṇākṛtīni ca

plain_english: See the Adityas, Vasus, Rudras, Ashvins, and Maruts, and many things never seen before; see wonders, O son of Pandu.
sanskrit_cite: paśyādityānvasūnrudrānaśvinau marutastathā | bahūnyadṛṣṭapūrvāṇi paśyāścaryāṇi pāṇḍava

plain_english: Here, in one place, see the whole world, moving and still, in my body, Guḍākeśa, and whatever else you wish to see.
sanskrit_cite: ihaikasthaṃ jagatkṛtsnaṃ paśyādya sacarācaram | mama dehe  guḍākeśa yaccānyad draṣṭumicchasi

plain_english: But you cannot see me with this own eye; I give you a divine eye: see my divine form.
sanskrit_cite: natu māṃ śakyase draṣṭumanenaiva svacakṣuṣā | divyaṃ dadāmi te  cakṣuḥ paśya me rūpamaiśvaram

plain_english: Saṃjaya said: having said thus, then, O king, Hari, the great lord of yoga, showed to Pārtha the supreme divine form.
sanskrit_cite: saṃjaya uvāca   evamuktvā tato rājan mahāyogīśvaro hariḥ | darśayāmāsa  pārthāya paramaṃ rūpamaiśvaram

plain_english: Many mouths and eyes, many wondrous sights; many divine ornaments; divine, many raised weapons.
sanskrit_cite: anekavaktranayanamanekādbhutadarśanam | anekadivyābharaṇaṃ  divyānekodyatāyudham

plain_english: Wearing divine garlands and garments, anointed with divine fragrance, full of all wonders, divine and endless, with faces everywhere.
sanskrit_cite: divyamālyāmbaradharaṃ divyagandhānulepanam | sarvāścaryamayaṃ  devamanantaṃ viśvatomukham

plain_english: If the splendor of a thousand suns were to rise at once in heaven, that might be like the splendor of that great soul.
sanskrit_cite: divi sūryasahasrasya bhavedyugapadutthitā | yadi bhāḥ sadṛśī sā  syādbhāsastasya mahātmanaḥ

plain_english: Then Arjuna saw the whole world, divided in many ways, in one place in the body of the god of gods.
sanskrit_cite: tatraikasthaṃ jagatkṛtsnaṃ pravibhaktamanekadhā | apaśyaddevadevasya śarīre pāṇḍavastadā

plain_english: Then Arjuna, filled with wonder, hair standing on end, bowed with his head and spoke to the god with folded hands.
sanskrit_cite: tataḥ sa vismayāviṣṭo hṛṣṭaromā dhanañjayaḥ | praṇamya  śirasā devaṃ kṛtāñjalirabhāṣata

plain_english: Arjuna said: I see your gods in your body, O god, and all groups of beings, Brahma the lord seated on the lotus, sages, and all divine serpents.
sanskrit_cite: arjuna uvāca   paśyāmi devāṃstava deva dehe sarvāṃstathā bhūtaviśeṣasaṅghān | brahmāṇamīśaṃ kamalāsanastha mṛṣīṃśca sarvānuragāṃśca  divyān

plain_english: I see you with many arms, bellies, faces, and eyes, endless in form on every side; I see no end, no middle, and no beginning again, O lord of the universe, universal form!
sanskrit_cite: anekabāhūdaravaktranetraṃ paśyāmi tvāṃ sarvato'nantarūpam | nāntaṃ na madhyaṃ na punastavādiṃ paśyāmi viśveśvara  viśvarūpa

plain_english: I see you crowned, mace-bearing, and discus-bearing, a mass of radiance on all sides, radiant; I see you hard to look at, all around, immeasurable in blazing fire, sun, and radiance.
sanskrit_cite: kirīṭinaṃ gadinaṃ cakriṇaṃ ca tejorāśiṃ sarvato dīptimantam | paśyāmi tvāṃ durnirīkṣaṃ samantā ddīptānalārkadyutimaprameyam

plain_english: You are the imperishable supreme to be known; you are the supreme treasury of this universe; you are imperishable, protector of sattvata dharma, eternal person, in my thought. Thus the principle known by those whose dharma is continuous grasping and renunciation, transcending all paths, is protected; this very secret in this chapter has mostly been revealed by me in the goddess-hymn commentary, and by those of like heart with instruction it is understood by itself. What again, by clearer manifestation and speech?
sanskrit_cite: tvamakṣaraṃ paramaṃ veditavyaṃ tvamasya viśvasya paraṃ nidhānam | tvamavyayaḥ sāttvatadharmagoptā sanātanastvaṃ puruṣo mato me | sāttvatadharmagopteti sat-satyaṃ-kriyājñānayorubhayorapi  bhedāpratibhāsātmakaṃ tathā sattātmakaṃ prakāśarūpaṃ tattvaṃ  vidyate yeṣāṃ te-sāttvatāḥ | teṣāṃ  dharmaḥ-anavaratagrahaṇasaṃnyāsaparatvātsṛṣṭisaṃhāraviṣayaḥ  sakalamārgottīrṇaḥ taṃ gopāyate | etadevātrādhyāye rahasyaṃ  prāyaśo devīstotravivṛttau mayā prakāśitam | tatsahṛdayaiḥ  sopadeśaiḥ svayamevāvagamyate iti kiṃ punaḥ punaḥ  sphuṭataraprakāśanavācālatayā

plain_english: I see you, infinite in power and arms, moon-and-sun-eyed, with a blazing fire-mouth, scorching this universe by your own radiance.
sanskrit_cite: anādimadhyāntamanantavīrya- manantabāhuṃ śaśisūryanetram | paśyāmi tvā dīptahutāśavaktraṃ svatejasā viśvamidaṃ tapantam

plain_english: Indeed, this interval between heaven and earth is pervaded by you alone, and all directions; seeing your wonderful fierce form, the three worlds are agitated, great soul.
sanskrit_cite: dyāvāpṛthivyoridamantaraṃ hi vyāptaṃ tvayaikena diśaśca sarvāḥ | dṛṣṭvādbhutaṃ rūpamugraṃ tavedṛ glokatrayaṃ pravyathitaṃ  mahātman

plain_english: Indeed these god-hosts enter into you; some frightened ones, with joined palms, praise, saying svasti; and great-sage hosts hymn you with abundant praises.
sanskrit_cite: amī hi tvā surasaṅghā viśanti kecidbhītāḥ prāñjalayo gṛṇanti | svastīti cottacaiva maharṣisaṅghāḥ stuvanti tvāṃ stutibhiḥ  puṣkalābhiḥ

plain_english: Rudras, Adityas, Vasus, Sādhyas, Viśve, Aśvins, Maruts, Uṣmapās, and Gandharva, Yakṣa, Asura, and Siddha hosts all behold you, astonished.
sanskrit_cite: rudrādityā vasavo ye ca sādhyā viśve'śvinau marutaścoṣmapāśca | gandharvayakṣāsurasiddhasaṅghā vīkṣante tvāṃ vismitāścaiva  sarve

plain_english: Seeing your great form with many mouths and eyes, mighty-armed, with many arms, thighs, feet, bellies, tusks, and fangs, the worlds are agitated, and so am I.
sanskrit_cite: rūpaṃ mahatte bahuvaktranetraṃ mahābāho bahubāhūrupādam | bahūdaraṃ bahudaṃṣṭrākarālaṃ dṛṣṭvā lokāḥ  pravyathitāstathā'ham

plain_english: Seeing you, whose form touches the sky, blazing in many colors, with open mouth and blazing wide eyes, my inner self is agitated; I find neither steadiness nor peace, O Viṣṇu.
sanskrit_cite: nabhaḥspṛśaṃ dīptamanekavarṇaṃ vyāttānanaṃ  dīptaviśālanetram | dṛṣṭvā hi tvāṃ pravyathitāntarātmā  dhṛtiṃ na vindāmi śamaṃ ca viṣṇo

plain_english: Seeing your fang-terrifying mouths, like death-fire, I know no directions and find no comfort; be gracious, lord of gods, abode of the world.
sanskrit_cite: daṃṣṭrākarālāni ca te mukhāni dṛṣṭvaiva kālānalasannibhāni | diśo na jāne na labhe ca śarma prasīda deveśa jagannivāsa

plain_english: All these sons of Dhritarashtra, together with groups of earth-protectors, Bhishma, Drona, that charioteer's son, and our own warrior chiefs, are seen.
sanskrit_cite: amī sarve dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putrāḥ sarve sahaivāvanipālasaṅghaiḥ | bhīṣmo droṇaḥ sūtaputrastathāsau sahāsmadīyairapi  yodhamukhyaiḥ

plain_english: Hurrying, they enter your fang-terrifying fearful mouths; some are seen stuck between the teeth with crushed heads.
sanskrit_cite: vaktrāṇi te tvaramāṇā viśanti daṃṣṭrākarālāni bhayānakāni | kecidvilagnā daśanāntareṣu sandṛśyante cūrṇitairuttamāṅgaiḥ

plain_english: Men of various forms, being crushed, enter your mouth of inconceivable form; Yudhishthira's and Dhritarashtra's warriors, all cut by various weapons, enter indeed.
sanskrit_cite: nānārūpaiḥ puruṣairbādhyamānā viśanti te vaktramacintyarūpam | yaudhiṣṭhirā dhārtarāṣṭrāśca yodhāḥ śastraiḥ kṛttā  vividhaiḥ sarva eva

plain_english: Surely these are slain by your radiance; for thus these have entered your body, as many river currents flow toward the ocean indeed.
sanskrit_cite: tvattejasā nihatā nūnamete tathāhīme tvaccharīre praviṣṭāḥ | yathā nadīnāṃ bahavo'mbuvegāḥ samudramevābhimukhā vajranti

plain_english: Thus your world-heroes enter the blazing mouths around, as moths enter blazing fire for destruction with swift force; so too worlds enter your mouths for destruction with swift force.
sanskrit_cite: tathā tavāmī naralokavīrā viśanti vaktrāṇyabhito jvalanti | yathā pradīptaṃ jvalanaṃ pataṅgā viśanti nāśāya  samṛddhavegāḥ | tathaiva nāśāya viśanti lokā stavāpi vaktrāṇi  samṛddhavegāḥ

plain_english: You lick and devour all worlds on every side with blazing mouths; filling the whole world with radiance, your fierce rays scorch, O Viṣṇu.
sanskrit_cite: lelihyase grasamānaḥ samantā llokānsamagrānvadanairjvaladbhiḥ | tejobhirāpūrya jagatsamagraṃ bhāsa stavogrāḥ pratapanti viṣṇo

plain_english: Tell me who you are, fierce-formed one; homage to you, best of gods, be gracious. I wish to know you, the primal one, for I do not know your course; I do not know why such a fierce form arises.
sanskrit_cite: ākhyāhi me ko bhavānugrarūpo namo'stu te devavara prasīda | vijñātumicchāmi bhavantamādyaṃ na hi prajānāmi tava pravṛttim | tava pravṛttiṃ na vedmi-kenāśayenedṛśīyamugrateti

plain_english: The blessed Lord said: I am Time, grown and world-destroying; I am engaged here to gather worlds. Even without you, all warriors stationed in opposing ranks will not be.
sanskrit_cite: śrībhagavānuvāca   kālo'smi lokakṣayakṛtpravṛddho llokānsamāhartumiha pravṛttaḥ | ṛte'pi tvā na bhaviṣyanti sarve ye'vasthitāḥ pratyanīkeṣu  yodhāḥ

plain_english: Therefore rise, gain glory; having conquered enemies, enjoy prosperous rule. These have already been slain by me; be a mere instrument, left-handed archer.
sanskrit_cite: tasmāttvamuttiṣṭha yaśo labhasva jitvā śatrūnbhuṅkṣva rājyaṃ  samṛddham | mayaivaite nihatāḥ pūrvameva nimittamātraṃ bhava  savyasācin

plain_english: Slay Droṇa, Bhīṣma, Jayadratha, Karṇa and other world-heroes; they have been slain by me, so do not be distressed; fight, and you will conquer rivals in battle. This here is the Lord's reply concerning the world's knowing-and-unknowing self; it is said that from pure, impure, and mixed awareness there is devouring. You fed the secret summarized in this chapter; may it be for those capable of immediate awareness. How much labor of line-writing; may we rest in stability. Here what was said by me: when they are slain, you, glorious one, be instrument. Thus by the Lord that was replied to what was said earlier by Arjuna: we do not know this; which of us is greater, and so on.
sanskrit_cite: droṇaṃ ca bhīṣmaṃ ca jayadrathaṃ ca karṇaṃ tathānyānapi  lokavīrān | mayā hatāṃstvaṃ jahi mā vyathiṣṭhā yudhyasva  jetāsi raṇe sapatnān | tadatra bhagavatottaraṃ jagato vidyāvidyātmanaḥ  śuddhāśuddhamiśrasaṃvidvalagrāsīkārādabhidhīyate-iti  prāśayaḥ sūtritamatrādhyāye rahasyam  uṭṭaṅkitamātrasaṃvittisamarthebhyo'stu | kiyatpaṃktilekhanāyāsadauḥ sthityamālambhemahi | atra yaduktaṃ  mayā hateṣu tvaṃ nimittaṃ yaśasvī bhava iti-bhagavatā  tatpratyuktaṃ yaduktaṃ prāgarjunena naitadvidbhaḥ katarannoḥ  garīyaḥ-ityādi

plain_english: Sañjaya said: having heard this speech of Keśava, the crowned one, with folded hands and trembling, bowed again and indeed said to Kṛṣṇa with faltering voice, greatly frightened, having prostrated.
sanskrit_cite: saṃjaya uvāca   etacchrutvā vacanaṃ keśavasya kṛtāñjalirvepamānaḥ kirīṭī | namaskṛtvā bhūya evāha kṛṣṇaṃ sagadgadaṃ bhītabhītaḥ  praṇamya

plain_english: Arjuna said: 'It is fitting, Hrishikesha, that by your praise the world rejoices and delights; frightened demons flee in all directions; and groups of siddhas bow.'
sanskrit_cite: arjuna uvāca   sthāne hṛṣīkeśa tava prakīrtyā jagatprahṛṣyatyanurajyate ca | rakṣāṃsi bhītāni diśo dravanti sarve namasyanti ca  siddhasaṅghāḥ | prakīrtyā-prakīrtanena

plain_english: Why do these not bow to the greater first creator Brahman? Because you, endless lord of gods and abode of the world, are the imperishable beyond true and false; false appearance is not an object as true meaning; or even nonbeing, joined to its own distinctive word and attaining knowledge-form, is not other than supreme Brahman-being; and that form is perceived in the concealment of both true and false cognition.
sanskrit_cite: kasmāccaite na nameyurmahātman garīyase brahmaṇo'pyādikartre | ananta deveśa jagannivāsa tvamakṣaraṃ sadasattatparaṃ yat | sat-padārthatvena | asat-upalambhaṃ pratyaviṣayatvāt | athavā  abhāvo'pi dhiyi nijanijaviśiṣṭavācakasaṃśleṣito  jñānākāramaśnuvāno na parabrahmasattāvyatiriktaḥ | sadasadrūpābhyāṃ ca param-tadubhayabuddhitirodhāne  tadrūpopalabdheḥ

plain_english: You are the primordial god, the ancient person; you are the supreme treasure of this universe; you are the knower and the knowable, the supreme abode; by you the universe of infinite form is pervaded.
sanskrit_cite: tvamādidevaḥ puruṣaḥ purāṇa stvamasya viśvasya paraṃ nidhānam | vettā'si vedyaṃ ca paraṃ ca dhāma tvayā tataṃ viśvamanantarūpam

plain_english: You are air, Yama, fire, Varuna, the moon, Prajapati, and great-grandfather; beginningless, measureless, unmatched being; lord of all; O all-great manifestation.
sanskrit_cite: vāyuryamo'gnirvaruṇaḥ śaśāṅkaḥ prajāpatistvaṃ  prapitāmahaśca | anādimānapratimabhāvaḥ sarveśvaraḥ  sarvamahāvibhūte

plain_english: Arjuna repeatedly salutes the lord from every side; through praise the lord's own form becomes directly perceptible, so further commentary is stopped to avoid repetition.
sanskrit_cite: namo namaste'stu sahasrakṛtvaḥ punaśca bhūyo'pi namo namaste | namaḥ purastādatha pṛṣṭhataste namo'stu te sarvata eva sarva | namo namaḥ-ityanena paunaḥ punyaṃ bhaktyatiśayāviṣkārakam yadeva  bhagavatātikrantādhyāyairabhyadhāyi svasvarūpaṃ tadevārjunaḥ  pratyakṣopalambhaviṣayāpannaṃ stotradvāreṇa prakaṭayatīti  tadvyākhyānaṃ kevalaṃ paunaruktyaprasaṅgāyeti viramyate

plain_english: No other is seen in the three worlds; the lord of inconceivable action, endless vigor, and unmeasured valor pervades all, therefore he is all.
sanskrit_cite: nahi tvadanyaḥ kaścidapīha deva lokatraye dṛśyate'cintyakarmā | anantavīryo'mitavikramastvaṃ sarvaṃ samāpnoṣi tato'si sarvaḥ

plain_english: Thinking you were my friend, I spoke forcibly, O Krishna, O Yadava, O friend; not knowing your greatness, I did this by carelessness or affection.
sanskrit_cite: sakheti matvā prasabhaṃ yaduktaṃ he kṛṣṇa he yādava he sakhe ca | ajānatā mahimānaṃ tavemaṃ mayā pramādātpraṇayena vāpi

plain_english: Whatever disrespect was shown to you for mockery, in play, bed, seat, or food, alone or before others, O Acyuta, I beg your pardon, immeasurable one.
sanskrit_cite: yaccāvahāsārthamasatkṛto'si vihāraśayyāsanabhojaneṣu | eko'thavāpyacyuta tatsamakṣaṃ tatkṣāmaye tvāmahamaprameyam

plain_english: You are father of the moving and still world, venerable teacher of this universe; none is equal to you, much less superior, in the three worlds of unmatched splendor.
sanskrit_cite: pitāsi lokasya carācarasya tvamasya viśvasya gururgarīyān | na  tvatsamo'styabhyadhikaḥ kuto'nyo lokatraye'pyapratimaprabhāva

plain_english: Therefore bowing and placing my body, I propitiate you, worshipful Lord; as a father bears a son, as a friend bears a friend, O god, you should endure.
sanskrit_cite: tasmātpraṇamya praṇidhāya kāyaṃ prasādaye tvāmahamīśamīḍhyam | piteva putrasya sakheva sakhyuḥ priyaḥ priyāsyārhasi deva soḍhum

plain_english: The sages remember your divine and wondrous former deeds; no other is doer of the world; you alone are sustainer, ordainer, and all-pervading Bhava.
sanskrit_cite: divyāni karmāṇi tavādbhutāni pūrvāṇi pūrve ṛṣayaḥ smaranti | nānyo'sti kartā jagatastvameko dhātā vidhātā ca vibhurbhavaśca

plain_english: What wondrous thing of yours would be unbearable, or what could be possible from another? I will proclaim, since you are doer of all, O vibhu; therefore all this is you alone.
sanskrit_cite: tavādbhutaṃ kiṃ nu bhavedasahyaṃ kiṃ vā śakyaṃ parataḥ  kīrtayiṣye | kartāsi sarvasya yataḥ svayaṃ vai vibho tataḥ  sarvamidaṃ tvameva

plain_english: Your action is extremely wondrous and not difficult; no comparison for your action is found; not even your qualities have measure, nor your splendor, strength, or glory.
sanskrit_cite: atyadbhutaṃ karma na duṣkaraṃ te karmopamānaṃ nahi vidyate te | nate guṇānāṃ parimāṇamasti na tejaso nāpi balasya narddheḥ

plain_english: Having seen this never-before-seen form, I am rejoiced and my mind is greatly distressed by fear; show me that very form, O god, be gracious, O lord of gods, abode of the world.
sanskrit_cite: adṛṣṭapūrvaṃ hṛṣito'smi dṛṣṭvā bhayena ca pravyathitaṃ mano  me | tadeva me darśaya deva rūpaṃ prasīda deveśa jagannivāsa

plain_english: I desire to see you crowned, mace-bearing, discus in hand; just so, by that very four-armed form, O thousand-armed one, be, O world-form.
sanskrit_cite: kirīṭinaṃ gadinaṃ cakrahasta- micchāmi tvāṃ draṣṭumahaṃ  tathaiva | tenaiva rūpeṇa caturbhujena sahasrabāho bhava viśvamūrte

plain_english: The blessed Lord said: by me, being gracious, this supreme form was shown to you, Arjuna, by self-yoga; radiant, world, infinite, primal, which by other than you has not been seen before.
sanskrit_cite: śrībhagavānuvāca   mayā prasannena tavārjunedaṃ rūpaṃ paraṃ darśitamātmayogāt | tejomayaṃ viśvamanantamādyaṃ yanme tvadanyena na dṛṣṭapūrvam

plain_english: Not by Veda, sacrifice, study, nor by gifts, nor by rites, nor by severe austerities can such a form be seen by me in the human world by other than you, O Kuru hero.
sanskrit_cite: na vedayajñādhigamanairna dānai- rna ca kriyābhirna tapobhirugraiḥ | evaṃrūpaṃ śakyamāhaṃ nṛloke draṣṭuṃ tvadanyena kurupravīra

plain_english: Let there be no distress for you, nor confusion, having seen this terrible fierce form of mine; with fear gone and pleased mind, again you behold that very gentle form of mine.
sanskrit_cite: mā te vyathā mā ca vimūḍhata bhūd dṛṣṭvā rūpaṃ ghoramugraṃ  mamedam | vyapetabhīḥ prītamanāḥ punastvaṃ tadeva me rūpamidaṃ  prapaśya

plain_english: Sanjaya said that Vasudeva, having spoken thus to Arjuna, showed his own form again, consoled the frightened one, and became the great soul of gentle form.
sanskrit_cite: saṃjaya uvāca   ityarjunaṃ vāsudevastathoktvā svakaṃ rūpaṃ darśayāmāsa bhūyaḥ | āśvāsayāmāsa ca bhītamenaṃ bhūtvā punaḥ saumyavapurmahātmā

plain_english: Arjuna said that having seen this gentle human form of Krishna, he is now restored, of sound mind, and returned to his nature; at the end of total withdrawal the Lord gives the supremely peaceful form, the state of Brahman-principle, and thus in conclusion the Lord's gentleness.
sanskrit_cite: arjuna uvāca   dṛṣṭvedaṃ mānuṣaṃ rūpaṃ tavasaumyaṃ janārdana | idānīmasmi  saṃvṛttaḥ sacetāḥ prakṛtiṃ gataḥ | sakalopasaṃhārānte paramapraśāntarūpāṃ brahmatattvasthitiṃ  dadāti-ityupasaṃhāre bhagavataḥ saumyatā

plain_english: The blessed Lord said: this form of mine that you have seen is very hard to see; even the gods always desire to see this form.
sanskrit_cite: śrībhagavānuvāca   sudurdarśamidaṃ rūpaṃ dṛṣṭavānasi yanmama | devā apyasya  rūpasya nityaṃ darśanakāṅkṣiṇaḥ

plain_english: I am not to be seen in such a form by the Vedas, nor by austerity, nor by gift, nor by sacrifice; you have seen me as I am.
sanskrit_cite: nāhaṃ vedairna tapasā na dānena na cejyayā | śakya evaṃvidho  draṣṭuṃ dṛṣṭavānasi māṃ yathā

plain_english: By undivided devotion I can be known, seen, and entered in truth in such a form, O Arjuna, scorcher of foes.
sanskrit_cite: bhaktyā tvananyayā śakya hyahamevaṃvidho'rjuna | jñātuṃ  draṣṭuṃ ca tattvena praveṣṭuṃ ca parantapa

plain_english: He who does my works, is devoted to me, is free from attachment, and is without enmity toward all beings reaches me, O Pandava. For those whose devotion shines forth toward no other knowable pleasant thing, Vasudeva approaches them; all. From the wonder of the previously stated teaching, the world-souled Vasudeva-principle descends effortlessly into the path of knowing. Auspicious. 60.
sanskrit_cite: matkarmakṛnmatparamo madbhaktaḥ saṅgavarjitaḥ | nirvairaḥ  sarvabhūteṣu yaḥ sa māmeti pāṇḍava | avidyamānānyajñeyaramaṇīyā yeṣāṃ bhaktiḥ parisphurati teṣāṃ  māṃ prapadyate vāsudevaḥ sarvam  ityādipūrvābhihitopadeśacamatkārāt viśvātmakaṃ  vāsudevatattvamayatnata eva bodhapadavīmavataratīti śivam

plain_english: Here is the summary verse: through recognition of the unity of consciousness arising from pure, impure, and mixed states, the sage who sees earth, midworld, and the three worlds with equality is equal.
sanskrit_cite: atra saṃgrahaślokaḥ   śuddhāśuddhavimiśrotthasaṃvidaikyavimarśanāt | bhūrbhuvaḥ  svastrayaṃ paśyansamatvena samo muniḥ | iti śrīmahāmaheśvarācāryavaryarājānakābhinavaguptapādaviracite  śrīmadbhagavadgītārthasaṃgrahe ekādaśo'dhyāyaḥ
